subject: High latency and 5xxs during peak — apparent hot-lane queueing (KV cache settings)
messages:
From: Alex Rodriguez <arod@acmecorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike (p99 ~1.2s -> 6.8s) and elevated 500 rate

Hi Priyom / Marissa —

We hit repeated user-facing latency spikes and a jump in 500s during our afternoon peak window yesterday (approx 15:00-16:30 PDT). Frontend metrics show request queue depth on your inference endpoints rising sharply and a correlated increase in KV cache misses for a subset of our long-running sessions. Attached is a p99 trace and a sample request stream.

Key impact: several web sessions experienced degraded chat responsiveness (users reported ~5–7s responses) and a 2.3% increase in 500s for the tier-1 API route. This is causing support tickets to back up.

We’d like:
- Brief root-cause hypothesis and immediate mitigation steps (within 4 hours)
- ETA for a durable fix and whether a config rollback is possible
- Request for SLA credit given customer impact (see attached SLA-request.pdf)

Thanks —
Alex
Product Ops, AcmeCorp
Attachment: p99_trace.png (image/png)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rodriguez <arod@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike (p99 ~1.2s -> 6.8s) and elevated 500 rate

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and the trace. I'm escalating immediately. Initial read: behavior looks like head-of-line (HOL) blocking in the online request queue where a small set of "hot" sessions are causing excessive KV cache churn and preventing batching from keeping lanes full. That combination can drive high tail latency and transient 5xxs under load.

Immediate actions we are starting now:
- Engaging infra: Rishi is running a targeted sampling to identify hot session keys and measure KV miss ratios.
- Rolling a safe config change: reduce per-lane max concurrent inflight (soft cap) and temporarily increase small-response batching timeout to prevent long ops from starving lanes. This is a quick mitigation we can test in the next 30–60m.
- Preparing a knob rollback plan if the change impacts throughput.

I'll keep you updated with a concrete mitigation timeline within 1 hour. If this is business-critical we can schedule an immediate brief with our on-call infra lead.

— Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike (p99 ~1.2s -> 6.8s) and elevated 500 rate

Adding technical detail and a proposed patch: 

Observed: sampling and KV server metrics show a tiny set (~0.4% of sessions) producing ~12% of KV traffic and causing frequent evictions on popular shards. When eviction happens, runtime incurs long-tail cache warmups and batch assembly is disrupted (HOL). We also saw increased time-to-first-token for some lanes because those requests were waiting for slots.

Proposed immediate patch (safe & reversible):
1) Increase KV local TTL for session-prefix keys from 60s -> 180s for reads-only detected sessions (reduce churn).
2) Add a small per-session concurrency guard: allow at most 2 in-flight requests per session on hot-key candidates (config toggle).
3) Raise the batching window from 4ms -> 8ms for the affected route to allow more compact batches during transient noise.
4) Instrument a short-lived hot-key blacklist: requests from keys in the top 1% of tail contributors get routed to a dedicated lane to avoid HOL on the main shared lanes.

Risk: (1) longer TTL increases memory pressure on KV shards (monitor) — we'll deploy with conservative shard caps. (2) raising batching window may increase median latency slightly but should reduce p99.

Plan: deploy patch to a single dedicated shard + shadow routing for 15m, verify error rates and p99, then promote if stable. I can push the change in ~45m.

Attachments: kv-config.yaml (proposed), small sampling logs included inline.

— Rishi
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) Customer comms: Alex requested an ETA for a durable fix and an SLA credit. Can we commit to an interim mitigation ETA of ~60 minutes and a follow-up technical write-up within 24 hours? Please advise on credit path (Monica, can you engage finance?)
2) Exec visibility: flagging this as P1 for our on-call and account execs. If the mitigation does not reduce p99 within 30–45m we should consider an emergency canary rollback or capacity bump.

Alex / Emily — we'll start the conservative patch now (Rishi will push to a canary shard in ~45m). We'll update you after the canary verification with concrete timings and any impact. We will also share the postmortem and config diff.

— Priyom
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — canary succeeded, next steps

Quick update:

Canary (single shard / 15m) completed — result: p99 reduced from ~6.8s -> ~1.5s on canary traffic and 500 rate fell to baseline. Memory pressure on the canary shard rose but remained under our safety cap. Rishi's hot-key lane routing prevented HOL on the main lanes.

Next steps:
- Expand rollout to remaining shards in 3 waves over next 3 hours with monitoring gates.
- Ops commit: postmortem doc and config diff (will attach) within 24 hours.
- Finance will evaluate SLA credit; Monica will follow up with Alex directly.

Alex — apologies for the disruption. We'll share the postmortem and the short-term config changes that fixed the hot-lane blocking.

— Monica
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
